boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Ten no-admission museum activities at SDSU, built around named collections and exhibits.

cards.title: Compare Harvey Dunn works together
cards.subtitle: South Dakota Art Museum, SDSU campus
cards.notes: Meet in the galleries and choose one Dunn work each to discuss. Check with museum staff first if you hope to see a particular piece.
cards.short_summary: A no-admission art conversation centered on the museum’s Harvey Dunn holdings.
cards.evidence_claim: The South Dakota Art Museum lists the Harvey Dunn Collection among its collections and says admission is free for all.
cards.access_notes: Open Monday-Friday 10 a.m.-5 p.m., Saturday 10 a.m.-4 p.m., and Sunday noon-4 p.m.; closed Sundays January-March and state holidays. Specific works may not be on view.

cards.title: Talk through Oscar Howe’s paintings
cards.subtitle: South Dakota Art Museum, SDSU campus
cards.notes: Bring a friend and spend time with works by Yanktonai Sioux artist Oscar Howe. Ask staff about current display locations before planning around one work.
cards.short_summary: A free gallery visit focused on the museum’s Oscar Howe Collection.
cards.evidence_claim: The museum identifies its Oscar Howe Collection as 27 paintings and states that admission is free for all.
cards.source_title: South Dakota Art Museum Collections Highlights
cards.access_notes: Museum admission is free for all. Visit during posted museum hours; collection displays rotate, so confirm a particular artwork with staff.

cards.title: Share a visual-storytelling prompt
cards.subtitle: South Dakota Art Museum, SDSU campus
cards.notes: Use the Paul Goble collection as a starting point for a quiet sketch or story prompt, then compare observations without handling any artwork.
cards.short_summary: A free, low-key gallery activity around Paul Goble’s illustrations.
cards.evidence_claim: The South Dakota Art Museum lists the Paul Goble Collection among its collections and says free admission is available to everyone.
cards.access_notes: Admission is free for all. The museum advises visitors to contact it ahead of time to confirm whether a specific piece is on view.

cards.title: Study Marghab Linen designs
cards.subtitle: South Dakota Art Museum, SDSU campus
cards.notes: Look for pattern, color, and craft details in the Marghab Linens collection. Compare two designs aloud while keeping a respectful gallery voice.
cards.short_summary: A free museum hang centered on an internationally significant linen collection.
cards.evidence_claim: The museum says its Marghab Collection is the largest and most comprehensive collection of Marghab Linens in the world, and admission is free for all.
cards.source_title: South Dakota Art Museum Collections Highlights
cards.access_notes: Admission is free for all. Collections are displayed on a rotating basis; contact the museum before visiting for a particular object.

cards.title: Pick a print and compare reactions
cards.subtitle: South Dakota Art Museum, SDSU campus
cards.notes: Choose prints from the Cockerline Collection to discuss visual style and era. Use the gallery labels, then compare what caught each person’s attention.
cards.short_summary: A no-cost print-focused conversation in the museum galleries.
cards.evidence_claim: The museum describes the Cockerline Collection as 532 works by 204 artists and states that admission is free for all.
cards.source_title: Cockerline Collection | South Dakota Art Museum
cards.access_notes: Museum admission is free for all. Confirm current gallery display status with the museum if you are seeking this collection specifically.

cards.title: Spend time with Native American art
cards.subtitle: South Dakota Art Museum, SDSU campus
cards.notes: Visit with a friend, read the labels closely, and discuss one work’s materials or perspective. Treat cultural content and gallery rules with care.
cards.short_summary: A free museum visit engaging with the Native American Collection.
cards.evidence_claim: The museum says its Native American Collection includes more than 1,100 donated objects and states that admission is free for all.
cards.source_title: South Dakota Art Museum Collections Highlights
cards.access_notes: Admission is free for all. Collection objects may rotate; contact the museum to verify what is currently available in the galleries.

cards.entity_name: 1915 J. I. Case Steam Engine 65 hp
cards.title: Inspect the 1915 Case steam engine
cards.subtitle: South Dakota Agricultural Heritage Museum, SDSU campus
cards.notes: Meet at the engine, inspect its construction details, and use the exhibit information to compare early farm power with today’s equipment.
cards.short_summary: A free museum stop at a named, restored 1915 steam engine.
cards.evidence_claim: The Agricultural Heritage Museum identifies its 1915 65 hp J. I. Case Steam Engine and says it does not charge admission.
cards.source_title: 1915 J. I. Case Steam Engine 65 hp | Agricultural Heritage Museum
cards.access_notes: The museum states that it does not charge admission. Hours are Monday-Saturday 10 a.m.-5 p.m. and Sunday 1 p.m.-5 p.m.; Sundays are closed January-March and on state holidays.

cards.title: Read the Claim Shanty exhibit together
cards.subtitle: South Dakota Agricultural Heritage Museum, SDSU campus
cards.notes: Use the exhibit to trace how the Homestead Act shaped prairie settlement. Compare the interpretive details and identify one question to research afterward.
cards.short_summary: A free history-focused hang at the museum’s named claim-shanty exhibit.
cards.evidence_claim: The museum lists the South Dakota Claim Shanty as a permanent exhibit and says it does not charge admission.
cards.source_title: Exhibits | South Dakota Agricultural Heritage Museum
cards.access_notes: The museum does not charge admission. Visit during its posted public hours; the museum is closed Sundays January-March and on state holidays.

cards.title: Explore the Ag-Xploration Gallery
cards.subtitle: South Dakota Agricultural Heritage Museum, SDSU campus
cards.notes: Bring younger friends or family to try the gallery’s agriculture-themed interactive stations, including moving grain, gathering eggs, and the farmers market.
cards.short_summary: A free, hands-on museum gallery intended for children ages 1–6.
cards.evidence_claim: The museum lists Ag-Xploration Gallery as a permanent exhibit with interactive agriculture activities for children ages 1–6 and says it does not charge admission.
cards.source_title: Exhibits | South Dakota Agricultural Heritage Museum
cards.access_notes: The museum does not charge admission. This gallery is designed for ages 1–6; visit with an appropriate child companion and follow posted exhibit guidance.

cards.title: Learn about the Overby Brothers invention
cards.subtitle: South Dakota Agricultural Heritage Museum, SDSU campus
cards.notes: Start at the Overby Brothers exhibit and compare its explanation of mechanized corn harvesting with a modern harvesting process you know.
cards.short_summary: A free museum activity focused on a named agricultural-invention exhibit.
cards.evidence_claim: The museum lists Overby Brothers as a permanent exhibit about an invention that mechanized corn harvesting and says it does not charge admission.
cards.source_title: Exhibits | South Dakota Agricultural Heritage Museum
cards.access_notes: The museum does not charge admission. Public hours are Monday-Saturday 10 a.m.-5 p.m. and Sunday 1 p.m.-5 p.m., with Sunday closures January-March and state holidays.
